question: Can a Houdini heightfield define the default world, and what does it look like in the engine?
findings: An unaligned 314-cell footprint needed more than 256 coarse roots; the importer now widens worlds to whole 32-cell blocks of flat sea (40 roots).

The actor never received ground facing inland: planner requests were sorted by node key, so a 128-key load prefix held only fine visual terrain. Requests now keep priority order; the actor's ground arrives after 7 plans (about 6 s) instead of never.
Unready root balancing requested one blocked split per plan (4 plans); it now requests them all at once (1 plan).
Inland start view: 110 fps falling to about 79 fps as the cover grows past 1,300 patches (2560x1440 surface, 4x MSAA).
limitations: Mountains are 60-80 degree spires; 13% of land is steeper than 60 degrees.
No sand or rock textures: beaches and cliffs render as meadow with grass to the waterline.
Frames were captured once each with the landscape render repro; no interleaved performance comparison.
